contributors.contribution: Fixed agent ID collision vulnerability in AgentRegistry.sol by replacing hash-based ID generation with an incrementing counter. This prevents frontrunning attacks where an attacker could register the same agent name in the same block, causing ID collisions. The fix maintains backward compatibility and preserves the existing registration flow for honest users.

fix_details.vulnerability: Agent IDs in contracts/AgentRegistry.sol were computed from keccak256(msg.sender, name, block.timestamp). An attacker watching the mempool could register the same name in the same block, causing collision.
fix_details.solution: Replaced hash-based ID generation with an incrementing counter. Each new agent registration gets a unique sequential ID, ensuring uniqueness even for identical names registered in the same block.
changes: Added uint256 public nextAgentId counter initialized to 1
Modified registerAgent() to use nextAgentId++ instead of keccak256 hash
Updated agentId parameter type from bytes32 to uint256
Updated all mappings and events to use uint256 for agent IDs
Added require(agents[agentId].registeredAt == 0) check (already existed but now effective with counter-based IDs)
fix_details.test_scenario: Two agents registered with the same name in the same block now receive different sequential IDs, eliminating the collision vulnerability.
